In the story of three generations, contrasts are skillfully developed. Thirshendu Mukhopadhyay's long novel "Binoculars" is a uniquely beautiful narrative of human relationships full of diversity. At one end of this story of three generations stands the landlord Hemkant, and at the other end stands his grandson Dhruv. And in the middle is told the story of Krishnakanta, son of Hemkanta and father of Dhruva. The main song of this novel is a unique and sweet analysis of Krishnakant's long life from the perspective of two people. "Binoculars" has built a deep bridge between these three generations. Zamindar Hemkant is a man of calm nature and thoughtful nature but with an extraordinary personality The first part of the story tells about Hemkant Landlord Hemkant and Rangamoyi, a priest's daughter but a woman with a strong personality, unfold a different kind of love story, a song of deep love over achievement, desire, calculation. The strength of Hemkanta of weak mentality lies in Rangamoyi. In the second generation we find Hemkanta's son Krishnakanta An idealistic boy who, at a young age, becomes the equivalent of a god child with his combination of devotion, concentration, values ​​and courage. Acceptance of Brakshacharya and love for the Swadeshi movement took him forward to a greater life A devoted Swadeshi before Partition, Krishna Kant became a powerful and powerful politician after Partition. And at the end of the story, Dhruv sees a strange relationship between him and his wife Remi. A strange relationship developed in the combination of love, contempt, indifference, neglect and love. On the other hand, in this episode Dhruva's Bhavuk is portrayed as a being who considers his father Krishnakanta as his greatest enemy. A deep hatred for his father leads him to another life, the consequences of which his own wife, Remy, suffers the most Leaving aside everything else in this story of three generations, what emerges most profoundly and vividly is the deep bond between father and son. On the one hand, Hemkant loves his opposite-natured son Krishnakanta more than his own life Their father son relationship clearly shows how much a father can love his son above all else On the other hand Krishnakanta and Dhruva have the opposite relationship. Dhruva has a great hatred for his father. Which brings down the relationship between two fathers and sons Apart from the narrative of the three generations, this epic novel depicts the Swadeshi movement, zamindari system, partition and the post-partition conditions. In this huge story with many characters, each character tells a different story. However, above all else, the father-son relationship and the generation gap created by generation after generation is a sad and beautiful narrative that is the core of "Durbeen". Personally, I was impressed by the trio of characters of Krishnakanth, Hemkanth and Rangamoyi And where many girls fall in love with Dhruv, I honestly think that Dhruv's character is a character immersed in darkness. 6671367777fadb04620f69c9c2c1cd2105b05926: Misir Ali is a popular mystery character created by the famous Bangladeshi novelist Humayun Ahmed. Misir Ali stories are mysterious. Misir Ali's stories are not exactly detective stories, or killer-police chases like 'crime fiction' or 'thriller', but psychological, science-based and heavily logical stories that I like very much. In many cases it can be called a mystery story. Characteristically, Missi's character Ali is a stark contrast to Humayun Ahmed's other excellent creation, Himu. Young Himu is driven by anti-logic; On the other hand the elder Misir Ali followed pure logic. This reasoning helps Misir Ali to uncover the true nature of the mysterious world. Those stories are mirrored in each of Misir Ali's novels. Humayun Ahmed, as Misir Ali, embodies two contrasting traits 'logic' and 'emotion'. Miss Ali is a smoker. He smokes 'Fifty Five' brand cigarettes. But he often tries to quit smoking. His body is quite emaciated and diseased. His body is plagued with various diseases: the liver is almost completely useless. Pancreatic function is reduced, average blood content, heart rate drops. That is why, besides these difficult diseases, any common disease makes him very lazy. As a result, he often had to stay in the hospital due to incurable diseases and eventually he recovered. Misir Ali is a very rational person and equally brave. He does not hesitate to spend the night in a haunted place, but stays there so that he can explain the mystery. One of Misir Ali's many abilities is that he can easily locate anyone, especially people with addresses, even in unknown places. For this he takes refuge in telephone directory, car registration number, TV-wireless license number, police case report, surathal (postmortem) report of hospital morgue etc. Misir Ali is amazed by the wonders of nature but is very logical and believes that there is no such thing as mystery in nature. Misir Ali Dharma is also an atheist by faith. In the 6th chapter of "Devi", the first novel of Misir Ali series, he calls himself an atheist. However, in some places he is presented as a believer in the existence of God, i.e. a theist. Miss Ali is basically a lonely man, as he is portrayed in almost all the novels. But in the novel "Anya Bhuban" it is mentioned that Ali got married to Missi. But in later novels he is again presented as a lonely man. In this regard, the author himself admitted that "it was a big mistake". A character like Misir Ali is not acceptable as a married man. And to correct that mistake, the writer presented Misir Ali as lonely again in the subsequent novels. The result is what Missir Ali's character stands for: Missir Ali cherishes a deep sea of ​​love in her heart, but never finds anyone close enough to spread that love. Adolescent workman is mentioned at various times to convey the loneliness of Misir Ali, who is plagued by the loneliness of love. Eg: In the novel "Ami and Amra" there is a reference to a 15-16 year old maid named "Badu". In the stories 'Devi' and 'Nishithini' there was a maid named Hanifa. Misir Ali tries to teach education to such a maid. Again in the novel "Anya Bhuban" a maid named "Reba" is mentioned. Ali's character of Missi has become so popular with the readers that many people have started thinking of him as a flesh and blood person. Humayun Ahmed is often asked whether Misir Ali is based on a real character. Many people find the shadow of the writer in Miss Ali's character after receiving a negative answer. Humayun Ahmed himself replied in this regard. Today Humayun Ahmed is not among us, but he is alive among us through his writings. I like this book very much. Read more

In that source, the name Zaheer Raihan is certainly not unknown. Moreover, his name was discussed in the international arena because of a documentary called "Stop Genocide" produced by Zaheer Raihan about the brutality and genocide of the Liberation War. When it comes to Bengali literature and films, Zaheer Raihan's name definitely comes to mind. Just as he could make a story beautifully believable on paper, he was equally adept at presenting that story beautifully on the screen. In 1960, his first novel "Shes Bickeler Mey" was published. "Baraf Gala Nadi" is the fourth novel written by him. It was published in 1969. Story: Maryam, a girl from a lower-middle-class family, tries to contribute to the family by doing tutoring. His elder brother Mahmud continues to fight with his mind in an effort to survive in the journalism job. Father Hasmat Ali works as a petty clerk. It is not possible for the father alone to support the expenses of this huge family with mother Saleha Bibi, younger sister Hasina and two younger brothers Khokon and Dulu. So they have to fight the battle of life. They live in a dilapidated rented house in a dirty street. When it rains, water seeps from the roof. Place it on the floor and place the water. A few people cannot climb together on a shaky roof. If it breaks! The one Miriam teaches is Selina. Selina's family is quite rich. Selina's older sister's brother-in-law, Mansoor, follows Maryam regularly. Miriam notices the matter but does not care. Maryam still hasn't forgotten how a man named Jahed ruined her life. To her, "All men are equal. All just want to enjoy. Love has no value to them. No matter how many acts they can play to get the body!" On the other hand, Selina's mother Anisa is planning to marry Selina with Begum Mansoor. But Mansoor does not leave Mariam. Mahmud is the eldest son of the family. Despite being educated, they are not getting suitable jobs. It is not possible to make the family happy by doing little things. Mahmud, who grew up in a lower-middle-class family, harbors a kind of resentment towards the big people. He turns his financial incapacity into anger and takes it out on the big people. Peta Mahmud, who harbored a great ideal to change the society, gradually suffered a mental breakdown as he was hit hard by life. Family ties also seem to him to be meek and superfluous. One day Mahmud saw Mansoor, Selina and Anisa Begum with Maryam in Newmarket. Seeing his sister traveling in a big man's car, his mood rises. Back home, he asked his sister in a sarcastic voice. A family war ensues. "Is teaching done at Newmarket?" Maryam replied, "They were going to Newmarket, took me with them..." "Why did you go? The relationship with them is that of master and master. Teach their daughter and get money in return. Surely you don't get any extra money to accompany them to Newmarket?" Mother Saleha Bibi came forward after hearing her son's scream. After hearing everything, he took the girl's side. "What happened to him in Newmarket, what wrong did he do that you scold him?" "Don't come to talk about what you don't understand, mother. Why don't you go to Newmarket, you'll go a hundred times, but not with those big men's children." Mahmud says with some self-restraint. Saleha Bibi angrily asks, "Why are they not human?" "Where don't they take me? Why Newmarket, they won't even take me by motor to Sadarghat. They will take me to the other side of the Buriganga to see your daughter. They promised to increase the salary by 10 taka this month, did they increase it? You think I don't know them? All of them are unscrupulous." What will be the result of Maryam, Mansoor, Selina's relationship? Who is Zaheed? What happened to Zahid with Miriam? What is the future of Mahmud wearing a hard shell of disgust? Where is the destination of Hasmat Ali's family? To know these answers, you have to carefully read one of the most important novels of Bengali literature, 'Baraf Gala Nadi', with a lively mood. Review 'Baraf Gala Nadi' has been written by enlivening the setbacks, joys, pains and not-to-gets of a declining lower-middle class family. The novel gives an accurate idea of ​​the life of a lower-middle-class family in 1969. The characters in the novel do not appear to be Mackie. So ordinary, so real, so familiar that the reader does not have to suffer at all to mingle with the characters. Writer Zaheer Raihan has beautifully portrayed the realistic scenario with the touch of words. But some shortcomings remain. After finishing the novel, some questions may arise in the minds of conscious readers. But the answer may not be found in the novel. Things are implied to avoid spoilers. Still, by all accounts, 'Baraf Gala Nadi' has made its place among the readers as a resource of Bengali literature. b04dfab218f673ed545a4419a0316ec927cd3ae8: The Alchemist is a novel by Brazilian author Paulo Coelho first published in 1988. Originally written in Portuguese, it is a novel translated into many languages. It is an international bestseller allegorical novel. The Alchemist follows an Andalusian shepherd on a trip to the pyramids of Egypt, dreaming repeatedly of finding a treasure there. A book that everyone should read at least once. A book that will help you understand life. Without reading this book, it would not be possible to understand the lessons of life that can be found in the story. The Alchemist describes the journey of an Andalusian shepherd boy named Santiago. For a recurring dream, he asks a Romani woman in a nearby town about the meaning of the dream for predictions. The woman interprets the dream as a prophecy and says that Santiago will discover a treasure in the Egyptian pyramids. Early in his journey, he meets an old king, who asks him to sell his sheep, in order to provide food for his journey to Egypt. and introduced the concept of a legend. Upon first arriving in Africa, a man claims to be able to lead Santiago to the pyramids, taking away what money he made by selling his sheep in return. Santiago then works for a merchant and embarks on a long journey to earn enough money to complete his personal legend and go to the pyramids. On the way, the boy met an Englishman, who came in search of an alchemist, and continued to travel with him. When they reach the oasis, Santiago falls in love with an Arabian girl named Fatima, to whom he proposes marriage. He promised to do so only after completing his journey. Disappointed at first, he later learns that true love does not end, nor does one have to sacrifice one's personal destiny, because that is the truth. The boy then meets a wise alchemist who teaches him to realize his true self. Together, they risk a journey across the territory of warring tribes, where the boy is forced to demonstrate his oneness with the "spirit of the world" before he is allowed to move on, turning himself into a simom. When he begins digging with an eye on the pyramids, he is robbed again, but accidentally learns from the leader of the thieves that the treasure he seeks is in the ruined church where he dreamed. 642d2e8bcaba79d89dac229caea0f96b3d824989: 'The Old Man and the Sea' is a novel written by the famous American writer Ernest Hemingway during his stay in Cuba in 1951 and published in 1952. Although it is a very common story of a fisherman, Ernest Hemingway's 'The Old Man and the Sea' is basically the story of the life of the fisherman who did not give up. The story is like this - an old fisherman who lives in Cuba, despite his long experience of life in prison, it is known at the beginning of the story that he is continuous Couldn't catch a single fish for 84 days. But for him this failure is not really a failure but just another step in the battle of life. He decided that he would go to a distant ocean where there were many big fish. What you think is what you do. The very next day he went out to the far sea and saw the biggest marlin fish he had ever seen. A new dimension of the story begins with this fish. To this degree, a story is described of the gradual transformation of the fish into the prey, the sacrifice of the fisherman to catch the fish and the development between the hunter and the hunter during the hunt. There are only 2 main characters. The first main character is Santiago, who is a native of Cuba and a fisherman by profession, he has become very crooked due to age, but he has a pair of wonderful eyes that have no aging, no fatigue. Santiago's wife is dead and he is childless. Despite living in extreme poverty, he seems to be content with life. And the reason for this satisfaction is his vast knowledge about sea and fishing. He himself is very confident and optimistic. You know life is about fighting, not about winning. He went out with the boat for 84 days but could not catch a single fish. With this slander, he became the most unlucky fisherman in his jail district. But nothing could stop him. He hunted the biggest marlin fish alone. For 3 days continuously he fought with nature and his body to catch the biggest fish of his life. In the end, he was not so worried about whether he succeeded or failed, but his pair of blue eyes had dreams. Besides Santiago, another character in the novel is a boy named Manolin, who used to work on Santiago's boat. In the story, this boy is seen as a fan of Santiago. He used to take care of Santiago, arrange his food, bring him newspaper and happily tell stories of playing American basketball with Santiago from the old paper. Although it is a very small story, the author seems to have made the story much bigger. In addition to various descriptions of sea life, this story highlights the real purpose of human life - to fight for life, the relationship between human society and nature, love for nature, love for life. And the story of an old fisherman who does not give up has come up strongly which teaches us many things. For example: if one's goal is unwavering, it will be possible to cross all obstacles and reach the goal. A must read. Note, The Old Man and the Sea won the Pulitzer Prize for Literature in 1953 and the Nobel Prize in 1954. Read more
